questions.title: Greeting a New Programmer
questions.description:
Your very first Java program warm up. Read a name from input and print a two line greeting exactly as shown.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word: the name.

Output Format:
Hello, <name>!
Welcome to Java programming.

Constraints:
1 <= length of name <= 20
questions.sampleoutput1:
Hello, Ada!
Welcome to Java programming.
questions.sampleoutput2:
Hello, Ken!
Welcome to Java programming.
questions.output1:
Hello, Grace!
Welcome to Java programming.
questions.output2:
Hello, Linus!
Welcome to Java programming.
questions.output3:
Hello, Mia!
Welcome to Java programming.

questions.title: Literals and Computed Values
questions.description:
A quick drill on printing literals versus computed values. Read a word and an integer, then print four lines: the word as read, the count as read, the next count and double the count.

Input Format:
One line with a word and an integer separated by a space.

Output Format:
Word: <word>
Count: <count>
Next count: <count + 1>
Double count: <count * 2>

Constraints:
1 <= count <= 1000000
questions.sampleoutput1:
Word: Java
Count: 4
Next count: 5
Double count: 8
questions.sampleoutput2:
Word: Code
Count: 10
Next count: 11
Double count: 20
questions.output1:
Word: Loop
Count: 1
Next count: 2
Double count: 2
questions.output2:
Word: Class
Count: 250
Next count: 251
Double count: 500
questions.output3:
Word: Object
Count: 999999
Next count: 1000000
Double count: 1999998

questions.title: Quoted Echo Printer
questions.description:
Print a word wrapped in real double quote characters. Build the quote marks from a char that holds the quote character, then also report the word length.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word.

Output Format:
Line 1: the word wrapped in double quotes, for example "Java"
Line 2: Length: <number of characters in the word>

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 30

questions.title: Corner Shop Receipt
questions.description:
A corner shop uses a tiny Java program to print receipt slips for every sale. Read the item name and the quantity sold, then print the slip. The shop also tracks a restock level, computed as quantity + 10.

Input Format:
One line with the item name (a single word) and an integer quantity, separated by a space.

Output Format:
*** RECEIPT ***
Item: <item>
Quantity: <quantity>
Restock level: <quantity + 10>

Constraints:
1 <= quantity <= 500

questions.title: Student ID Card Printer
questions.description:
At college orientation, a desk assistant prints student ID cards using a simple Java program. Read the student first name and roll number, then print the card exactly as shown, including the separator lines made of equals characters.

Input Format:

Output Format:

questions.title: Conference Badge Generator
questions.description:
An event desk automates conference badges with a Java program. Read the attendee name, badge number and event code, then print the badge. The seat pass line is formed by joining the event code, a hyphen and the badge number.

Input Format:
One line with three tokens separated by spaces: name (a single word), badge number (an integer), event code (a single word).

Output Format:
====================
CONFERENCE BADGE
Name: <name>
Badge No: <badge>
Event: <eventCode>
Seat pass: <eventCode>-<badge>

1 <= badge number <= 100000

questions.title: Study Plan Tracker
questions.description:
An online platform tracks each learner journey through a 30 day Java plan. Read the student name on its own line, then the starting day and the number of days already completed, each on its own line. The plan always ends on day 30; report the end day and how many days remain.

Input Format:
Line 1: student name (may contain spaces)
Line 2: starting day (an integer)
Line 3: days completed (an integer)

Output Format:
Student: <name>
Plan: Day <start> to Day <end>
Days completed: <completed>
Days remaining: <30 - end>

Constraints:
1 <= start <= 29, 1 <= completed, start + completed <= 30

questions.title: App JVM Compatibility Checker
questions.description:
A deployment bot checks whether an app can run on the installed JVM before shipping. Read the app name, the JVM version the app requires and the installed JVM version. Print the check report; an upgrade is needed exactly when the installed version is lower than the required version.

Input Format:
One line with three tokens separated by spaces: app name (a single word), required JVM version (an integer), installed JVM version (an integer).

Output Format:
App: <app>
Required JVM: <required>
Installed JVM: <installed>
Upgrade needed: yes or no

Constraints:
1 <= required <= 100, 1 <= installed <= 100
questions.sampleoutput1:

Required JVM: 11
Installed JVM: 8
Upgrade needed: yes
questions.sampleoutput2:
App: ChatApp
Required JVM: 8
Installed JVM: 17
Upgrade needed: no

App: GameBox
Required JVM: 17
Installed JVM: 11

questions.output2:
App: NoteKeeper
Required JVM: 8
Installed JVM: 8
Upgrade needed: no
questions.output3:

questions.title: Sponsor Tier Report
questions.description:
An event finance tool sums sponsor contributions and assigns a partnership tier. Read the sponsor company name, the number of gold sponsors, the number of silver sponsors, the contribution per gold sponsor and the contribution per silver sponsor (all integers, in rupees). The base amount is goldCount * perGold + silverCount * perSilver. A bonus of one tenth of the base (integer division) is added. The tier is PLATINUM when the grand total is at least 100000, GOLD when it is at least 25000, otherwise SILVER.

Input Format:
One line with five tokens separated by spaces: company (a single word), goldCount, silverCount, perGold, perSilver (integers).

Output Format:
Sponsor: <company>
Base amount: <base>
Bonus amount: <base / 10>
Grand total: <base + bonus>
Tier: <PLATINUM or GOLD or SILVER>

Constraints:
0 <= goldCount, silverCount <= 1000, 1 <= perGold, perSilver <= 100000

Tier: GOLD

questions.title: Employee Joining Kit Card
questions.description:
HR prints a joining kit card for every new employee. Read the employee full name on its own line, then one line with the department code, desk number and floor number. The access code is floor * 1000 + desk. The zone letter comes from the floor: floors 1 to 3 are zone A, floors 4 to 6 are zone B, floors 7 to 9 are zone C.

Input Format:
Line 1: full name (may contain spaces)
Line 2: dept (a single word), desk (an integer), floor (an integer), separated by spaces

Output Format:
JOINING KIT
Employee: <name>
Dept: <dept>
Floor: <floor>
Desk: <desk>
Access code: <floor * 1000 + desk>
Zone: <A or B or C>

Constraints:
1 <= desk <= 999, 1 <= floor <= 9
